title: Transient KV-slot fragmentation + attention-tile crossover causing token alignment corruption
creator: Aisha Khatri
description: Summary: After recent performance changes to attention tiling and dynamic kernel selection, we are seeing rare correctness failures in long conditioning requests: token duplication/shift and silent output drift. Root cause appears to be a race between the conditioning-stage scheduler that evicts/compacts KV slots and a fast-path fused attention kernel that switches tiling layout mid-sequence. The layout switch changes accumulation/reduction order in vectorized softmax and combined with partial KV-slot compaction leads to stale KV references and numeric rounding differences that amplify into token misalignment. This ticket tracks investigation, short-term mitigations, and long-term fixes.
steps_to_reproduce: Start runtime-2.3 with dynamic-attention-tiling enabled (env VAR DYN_ATT_TILING=1)
Send a prefill of ~4k tokens followed by interleaved decode requests (mix of synchronous and streaming) to the same session so KV cache reaches >64K slots and triggers compaction
Force a kernel crossover by alternating sequences with short (<64) and long (>1024) decode lengths to exercise fused vs blocked kernels
Observe outputs for token duplication/shift or softmax-produced probability anomalies in logs (sampling diff vs baseline)
impact: High: observed on internal canary and reproduced deterministically in ~1/200 long-session runs. Affects hosted customers running long prompts and multi-turn chat; can produce subtle content corruption rather than crashes, making detection hard. Leads to hallucinations, token repeats, and context loss for affected sessions.
hypothesis: 1) The kernel selector may switch tiling/accumulation order when conditions change mid-session. 2) The KV-slot compaction code moves slot pointers without coordinating with in-flight kernels, producing stale reads. 3) Vectorized softmax in the fused kernel uses a different floating-point reduction associativity than the blocked kernel; when combined with stale KV fragments it produces numerical drift that changes beam/sampling decisions.
mitigations: Short-term: force single attention kernel per-session (disable dynamic crossover) via config flag to avoid mixed accumulation paths
Apply lightweight scheduler lock when compacting KV slots to block new kernel dispatches for sessions currently under compaction (quick patch)
Add detection: checksum of KV-region meta before/after compaction and emit alert if mismatch
Roll back vectorized softmax micro-optimizations that change reduction ordering while rollback patch is validated
test_plan: Create deterministic fuzz harness that reproduces the sequence that triggers the bug (see reproducer branch)
Add unit tests that assert KV slot pointer invariants across compaction boundaries
Add randomized float-order consistency tests comparing fused vs blocked kernels over long sequences with seeded RNG
Run 72h canary with the 'single-kernel-per-session' flag and monitor token-diff metric against baseline (dash: /dashboards/token-diff-long-population)
comments: 2026-03-10 - Aisha Khatri: Filed after customer canary spike. Attached reproducer and initial logs. Observed 3 distinct symptom patterns: repeated tokens, shifted context, and silent probability drift without repeats.

2026-03-11 - Marco Li: Confirmed local reproduction on GPU devbox using repro branch. Narrowed window: kernel crossover + KV compaction within same microsecond window. Started prototype compaction lock in PR 1782.

2026-03-11 - Priya Nambiar (runtime perf): Ran float-consistency comparison between fused and blocked softmax; found mean absolute difference ~2e-7 per element but worst-case accumulation diverged after repeated decoding (amplifies sampling changes).
2026-03-12 - SRE: Canary flagged ~0.5% of long sessions with token-diff > threshold; temporarily toggled dynamic-tiling off for canary clusters, customer impact dropped to 0.02%.
2026-03-12 - Marco Li: Implemented short-term single-kernel-per-session flag. Need to harden compaction lock and add KV meta checks. Planning to land lock as emergency patch after review.

2026-03-13 - Code review notes: Ensure lock is per-session and non-blocking for unrelated sessions; avoid introducing serialization for all compactions. Add metrics: compaction_wait_ms and compaction_conflicts_count.
